parts.title: Shadow Puppets In Southeast Asia
parts.article:
(A) In many cultures today, people view puppets as simply toys for children. In Southeast Asia, however, shadow-puppet theatre and shadow-puppet imagery, which date back some 1200 years, fulfil many roles — from ceremonial and ritual purposes to entertainment. Performances are usually held at night, and people of all ages and from all walks of life watch as a puppeteer creates shadow-plots by manipulating puppets between a light source and a white cloth screen, while simultaneously conducting the orchestra. The music highlights the action and dramatic moments, accompanies the singing and evokes appropriate moods.

(B) Shadow puppets are flat objects traditionally created from the skin of an animal that has been cleaned, stretched and dried. This usually comes from the skin of a buffalo or cow, but bear, deer and other animals are sometimes used too. The shape of the puppet is first drawn onto the skin and then cut out. Holes are punched all over the puppet to create the appearance and textures of the character's clothes. Finally these features are painted in and they are fitted with the rods the puppeteers use to move them. Puppeteers can have 200 or more puppets in their collections.

(C) While many of these puppets are generic, playing different roles as necessary, others represent specific characters, some of which have special status. These are treated accordingly, often being separately wrapped in cloth or thread, or kept with offerings such as flowers or money.

(D) Maintaining hierarchy and social organisation, and thus harmony, has always formed part of the conventions of shadow-puppet theatre. This is established through the performance itself, as well as through the stage set-up. For example, puppets are arranged with the honourable characters on the right of the screen, and more negative characters on the left; noble characters are placed close to the screen, and more mundane ones further away and so less clear to the audience. When placed in a travelling case, Thai puppets are traditionally organised with the animals and scenery on the bottom, and the sacred and royal figures on the top. Shadow-puppet theatre thus represents the surrounding universe, presenting its struggles between harmony and chaos in the performance and striving to achieve a balance between them. Individuals and communities still commission shadow-puppet theatre performances, often for major life transitions, such as marriage, as well as to celebrate the harvest and to fulfil vows.

(E) The plays performed today include stories that originated in India and travelled to Southeast Asia via trade routes, as well as locally developed stories based on characters from these narratives. More recently, completely original stories based on local events have emerged, in which the conventional balance between chaos and harmony is not necessarily established during the course of the performance. Stories are primarily performed orally, and puppeteers usually do not use a written script when performing. They rely instead on memorising basic stories, and often improvise during shows, inventing extra material as they go along. Electricity is now widely used to illuminate the screens, replacing candles or oil lamps in many performances. In some instances, electric instruments are played alongside earlier musical forms. While in Java and southern Burma, the theatre has successfully adapted to modern-day needs and interests, in Malaysia public performances have declined dramatically since the 1930s.

(F) Reinterpretations of stories and puppet imagery have resulted in the creation of interesting new forms. Thai puppets from the late 20th century are a particularly interesting example. Some of these present traditional forms, but are made of plastic instead of animal skin. Others obviously reflect the fashion of the era — for example Thai puppets, made of animal skin and with traditional body shapes, yet dressed in 1970s-type flared trousers and high-heeled shoes, are still to be found performing today.

(G) Shadow-theatre's popularity in Southeast Asian society has also led to its imagery and characters being adopted outside their original context. For instance, the legendary warrior figure known as Bima, which originated in India as a character in the epic poem Mahabharata, came to be widely revered beyond the world of puppet theatre as a symbol of strength, courage and righteousness over a thousand miles away in Java. Imagery related to the shadow-puppet form of Bima can still be found there on stone reliefs dating to the 1400s.

(H) Shadow-puppet characters and images have also appeared in many other settings. Coins and medallions with shadow-puppet figures on them were once worn in Malaysia and Indonesia as talismans. Today, shadow-puppet-theatre imagery and puppets form such an integral part of local culture that they are often used commercially. In Thailand, famous clown puppets have become part of local identity and are used in advertising campaigns. Mass media has made some puppeteers celebrities, and performances are now broadcast online. The use and reuse of shadow-theatre elements have a long history and continues to the present day.

reference:
Q1

解析 文章明确提到，在东南亚有各个年龄段、各行各业的人都会观看皮影戏，这就等同于吸引了广泛的观众。

干扰 你可能会漏掉原文中“people of all ages and from all walks of life”这个用来完美同义替换“a wide audience”的短语。

句子 In Southeast Asia, however, shadow-puppet theatre and shadow-puppet imagery, which date back some 1200 years, fulfil many roles — from ceremonial and ritual purposes to entertainment. Performances are usually held at night, and people of all ages and from all walks of life watch as a puppeteer creates shadow-plots by manipulating puppets between a light source and a white cloth screen, while simultaneously conducting the orchestra.

Q2

解析 文章详细举例了高尚的角色被放在屏幕右边或靠近屏幕，负面或普通角色放在左边或较远，说明屏幕上的位置确实能反映出角色性格。

干扰 你可能会因为没读懂“relative position”在文中具体指代“on the right/left”或“close to/further away”而不敢选择TRUE。

句子 This is established through the performance itself, as well as through the stage set-up. For example, puppets are arranged with the honourable characters on the right of the screen, and more negative characters on the left; noble characters are placed close to the screen, and more mundane ones further away and so less clear to the audience.

Q3

解析 原文提到泰国皮影放在旅行箱里时，传统上会把动物放下面、神圣人物放上面，这就是一种存放的习俗。

干扰 你可能会把题干中的“storage”（存放）和原文的“placed in a travelling case”（放在旅行箱里）对应不上而产生怀疑。

句子 When placed in a travelling case, Thai puppets are traditionally organised with the animals and scenery on the bottom, and the sacred and royal figures on the top.

Q4

解析 文章虽然提到了人们为了婚姻等人生大事雇人演皮影戏，但完全没提这方面是否获得了“日益增长的成功”（growing success）。

干扰 你可能会因为在文中看到了“marriage”就主观脑补皮影戏在婚礼上很受欢迎，而忽略了文章根本没有提及成功与否的趋势。

句子 Individuals and communities still commission shadow-puppet theatre performances, often for major life transitions, such as marriage, as well as to celebrate the harvest and to fulfil vows.

Q5

解析 原文说表演者在演出时经常会即兴发挥并编造额外的内容，这与题干说的遵循“固定情节”完全相反。

干扰 你可能会看到前面说他们“记住了基础故事”就以为是固定情节，从而忽略了紧随其后的“即兴发挥（improvise）”。

句子 Stories are primarily performed orally, and puppeteers usually do not use a written script when performing. They rely instead on memorising basic stories, and often improvise during shows, inventing extra material as they go along.

Q6

解析 题干问在剪下来之前要先创造什么，原文明确说皮影的“形状（shape）”是先画到皮上然后再剪下来的。

干扰 你可能没有注意到题干中“before cutting it out”和原文中“first drawn... then cut out”在时间顺序上的对应关系。

句子 The shape of the puppet is first drawn onto the skin and then cut out.

Q7

解析 原文说会在皮影上打出“孔洞（holes）”来展现角色衣服的外观和纹理，这正是题干中“添加细节”的具体动作。

干扰 你可能不认识“punched”（打孔）这个词，导致无法锁定答案就是被打出来的“holes”。

句子 Holes are punched all over the puppet to create the appearance and textures of the character's clothes.

Q8

解析 原文提到最后会给它们安装上表演者用来移动它们的“杆子（rods）”，对应的就是给皮影添加的东西。

干扰 你可能会被前面的“painted”（上色）干扰，但题干的“add”对应的是原文的“fitted with”，因此只能填“rods”。

句子 Finally these features are painted in and they are fitted with the rods the puppeteers use to move them.

Q9

解析 题干问什么被广泛用作光源，原文一字不差地写着“电力（Electricity）现在被广泛用于照亮屏幕”。

干扰 你可能会去选被替代掉的“candles”或“oil lamps”，而忽略了题干问的是现在被广泛使用的东西。

句子 Electricity is now widely used to illuminate the screens, replacing candles or oil lamps in many performances.

Q10

解析 原文提到在马来西亚（Malaysia），公开表演自20世纪30年代以来大幅下降，直接对应题干中的观众显著减少。

干扰 你可能会错填成前面成功适应现代需求的“Java”或“Burma”，没有看清句子前后的转折对比。

句子 While in Java and southern Burma, the theatre has successfully adapted to modern-day needs and interests, in Malaysia public performances have declined dramatically since the 1930s.

Q11

解析 题干问服装明显受到了那个时代的什么影响，原文直接给出了反映了那个时代的“时尚（fashion）”。

干扰 你可能会因为看到后面的“trousers”或“shoes”就想填具体衣服，但题目限制填一个词且概括性最高的是“fashion”。

句子 Others obviously reflect the fashion of the era — for example Thai puppets, made of animal skin and with traditional body shapes, yet dressed in 1970s-type flared trousers and high-heeled shoes, are still to be found performing today.

Q12

解析 题干问在泰国被用于商业上的什么方面，原文清晰指出泰国的著名小丑皮影被用在了“广告（advertising）”活动中。

干扰 你可能光看了第34句的“commercially”而没有接着往下读，从而找不到具体国家（Thailand）和对应的应用领域。

句子 Today, shadow-puppet-theatre imagery and puppets form such an integral part of local culture that they are often used commercially. In Thailand, famous clown puppets have become part of local identity and are used in advertising campaigns.

Q13

解析 题干问现在可以在哪里观看皮影戏，原文直接说明演出现在被在线（online）广播了。

干扰 你可能会被前半句的“mass media”吸引注意力，而没看到句末直接给出播出方式的真正答案。

句子 Mass media has made some puppeteers celebrities, and performances are now broadcast online.
